Subject: Hosted evaluation: deployment preferences & initial ops asks

Hi Sara —

Great to meet earlier — thanks for the time and for walking us through BrightCart's product flow. Quick recap + requests so we can provision a meaningful hosted sandbox and confirm whether Hosted API will meet your needs or if a Dedicated/Private path is required.

Recap from demo:
- Primary inference surface: product title + description rewriting + category classification (single-turn, deterministic).
- Expected traffic: see attached BrightCart_traffic_profile.xlsx (you mentioned growth scenarios).
- Compliance baseline: SOC 2 is in scope; data residency preference is US only.

Key ops/qualification items we need to finalize for Hosted evaluation:
1) Traffic profile: please confirm expected steady-state requests per second (RPS), expected tokens per request, and spike characteristics (duration/frequency).
2) Endpoints & rate limits: do you need per-route isolation (separate keys or routes) or can a single sandbox endpoint suffice for initial testing?
3) Networking: do you require inbound VPC peering or only allowlist of outbound egress destinations?
4) Security evidence & timeline: any procurement docs or questionnaire deadlines we should align to (SOC artifacts, encryption/KMS questions).

What we can provide for a Hosted pilot:
- A dedicated sandbox endpoint (regional, US) with staging keys and a default quota (20 RPS) and burst allowance; we can request higher caps after an initial smoke test.
- Prefix/KV caching to reduce token cost for rewrites; works well if you have repetition in prompts.
- Per-request token accounting and cost estimates after we get your traffic numbers.

Next steps I propose:
- Sara to confirm traffic numbers + security timeline (reply to this thread).
- Ben (SE) and Aditya (Infra) to scope network requirements and provide a sandbox provisioning plan.
- We’ll attach a short quickstart checklist (redwood_quickstart_checklist.pdf) to help your engineering team.

Attachments: redwood_quickstart_checklist.pdf, network_requirements.csv (sample)

Thanks — I’ll hold off on provisioning until I have the traffic numbers so we pick sensible defaults.

Best,

Hi Marissa —

Thanks for the concise recap — this is helpful. A few clarifications from our side so you can size the hosted sandbox and flag any blockers: 

Traffic profile (current / target):
- Steady state: ~50 RPS across our rewrite endpoint (mostly user-facing).
- Typical tokens per request: ~1,500 tokens (prompt + expected generated).
- Bursts: we see short spikes up to ~200 RPS for 20-40 seconds during promotional pushes; these are important for UX.

Routing / endpoints:
- For initial evaluation a single staging endpoint is fine, but for prod we expect separate routes for rewrite vs classification.

Networking / security:
- SOC 2 Type II is a requirement for procurement; we need to understand what artifacts you can provide and the timeline.
- Data residency: US-only required.
- We do not have a VPC peering requirement for proof-of-concept, but ultimately we prefer a model where outbound calls to internal telemetry services go over peered/private networking. Is VPC peering supported from Hosted?

Attachments: I’ve included BrightCart_traffic_profile.xlsx with traffic slices and peak windows.

If you can confirm the sandbox quota and whether Hosted supports VPC peering (or if that pushes us to Dedicated/Private), we can schedule a technical follow-up with engineering this week. Available windows: Thu 8/17 10:00–12:00 PT or Fri 8/18 13:00–15:00 PT.

—Sara

Hi Sara —

Thanks — the traffic profile helps a lot. A few clarifications and our recommended path: 

1) Hosted pilot feasibility given numbers you provided:
- Steady 50 RPS @ ~1.5k tokens: Hosted can handle this in the US region. Token cost and latency will depend on batching and your chosen model; we’ll produce a cost estimate once we pick model/quantization.
- Bursts to 200 RPS (20–40s): Hosted can absorb short bursts but the default sandbox quota (20 RPS) will need to be raised for meaningful load tests. We can provision a pilot sandbox with a higher quota (proposed 100 RPS burst-capable) for a 14-day pilot; permanent higher limits typically require Dedicated or a committed plan.

2) VPC peering / private networking:
- Hosted API does not support customer-initiated VPC peering for inbound peering today. For private connectivity (VPC peering, private endpoints, or on-prem), our Dedicated or Private options are the right path.
- For Hosted you can allowlist outbound egress to our regional endpoints (*.redwoodapi.com over 443). If you need telemetry to flow to internal services behind your VPC, that will require Dedicated/Private or a short-term workaround (webhook proxy inside your VPC).

3) Security artifacts:
- We can provide SOC 2 Type II summary and our controls doc; our security team can work with your procurement on an NDA and an initial evidence package. Please share the procurement timeline and any specific questionnaire link if you have one.

4) Quickstart & sandbox provisioning:
- We can provision a staging endpoint scoped to BrightCart with: 100 RPS soft quota, regional US endpoint, staging keys, and prefix/KV cache enabled.
- Proposed pilot length: 14 days for performance and cost estimates. After the pilot we’ll review metrics and propose next steps (Hosted scaling vs Dedicated).

Next steps:
- Sara to confirm which pilot window you prefer (Thu 8/17 or Fri 8/18).
- Ben & Aditya to confirm technical readiness items for sandbox (ports, allowlist, token lifecycle).
- I’ve attached a short ops doc that spells out the quickstart steps and what we need from your infra team (hosted_quickstart_ops.md).

Links: HubSpot deal: https://app.hubspot.com/contacts/12345/deal/BR-2028-091

Thanks —

Hi Sara —

Quick technical answers and a suggested validation plan from the SE side.

Rate / quotas:
- Default sandbox quota: 20 RPS.
- We can provision a temporary pilot sandbox with a soft quota of 100 RPS and burst accommodation to ~200 RPS for short windows (as you described) for a 14-day pilot. Permanent increases require capacity planning/commit.

Latency & tokens:
- With ~1.5k tokens, expect 200–400ms per-token execution variance depending on model and concurrency at the time of the call; we'll instrument latency and tail-percentiles in the pilot.

Cost control techniques to validate in pilot:
- Prefix/KV caching for rewrite workloads to cut repeated prompt tokens.
- Response length caps and token limits to bound cost.
- Batching at the client if you can tolerate slight latency (we can demonstrate tradeoffs).

Network allowlist / ports:
- Hosted endpoints are HTTPS only. Allowlist: outbound to *.redwoodapi.com (443). No inbound ports required.

Validation plan (suggested):
1) We provision sandbox (100 RPS soft quota) and share staging keys + endpoint.
2) Run a 48-hour soak at steady 50 RPS to validate stability and gather cost/latency.
3) Execute 3 controlled bursts (200 RPS, 30–40s) to observe bursting behavior.
4) Review metrics with you and decide whether to continue on Hosted or scope Dedicated for production (if sustained higher capacity or VPC peering is required).

If you confirm the Fri 8/18 13:00 PT slot I’ll be on the call to walk through the sandbox provisioning and network steps.
